requirements.title: kP temporarily sets the scale factor for real and complex numeric editing
requirements.definition: kP temporarily changes the connection scale factor to k, affecting F, E, EN, ES, EX, D, and G editing for real and complex quantities.

pending.scale-factor-affects-real-complex: WRITE(buf,'(1P,F5.1)') 1.0; expect exactly ' 10.0' for the real scalar case; complex pair coverage is deferred until complex numeric editing ownership.

requirements.title: The scale factor has distinct input and output effects for F/E/D/G/EN/ES/EX editing
requirements.definition: Scale factor multiplies/divides external decimal values for eligible input without exponents, has no input effect when an exponent exists, scales F output, adjusts E/D significand and exponent, is suspended for G unless E editing is required, and has no output effect for EN/ES/EX.

pending.input-no-exponent-external-equals-intern: READ('10.0','(1P,F4.1)') into a real variable; expected mathematical value is 1.0.
pending.input-exponent-no-scale-effect: READ('1.0E+1','(1P,E6.1)') into a real variable; expected mathematical value is 10.0 because the exponent suspends input scale effect.
pending.E-D-output-significand-and-exponent-adju: Deferred exact output to E/D editing owners; future fixture must state exact significand and exponent characters after applying k.
pending.G-output-scale-suspended-unless-E-requir: WRITE(buf,'(3P,G9.2)') 0.0; expect exactly '  0.0    ', the same as unscaled G9.2 zero because G uses F editing for this magnitude.
pending.EN-ES-EX-output-no-scale-effect: Deferred exact output to EN/ES/EX owners; future paired controls with and without kP must state exact identical fields before execution.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, two rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_138.json. The reviewer re-derived the receipt (21 sections, 64 units, 0 hash mismatches) and INDEPENDENTLY RE-PARTITIONED the four crowded pages - p303, p304, p306 and p307 - unit by unit, confirming among other things that 13.8.8 genuinely owns only p1 despite covering six rounding-mode descriptors. A mis-attributed paragraph would have been invisible in the totals, since 64 would still be 64. The zero-numbered-R/C claim was verified: R1323 appears on p302 but belongs to the sibling 13.7.2.4 packet. FOUR blocking findings, all closed. C138SR-001: a negative was filed against 13.7.5.2.2, which only CROSS-REFERS to the rule - the actual prohibition is 13.7.5.1 p1 'On input, w shall not be zero' - and 'Note that w cannot be zero' is a reminder, not a prohibition; the facet is now an explicit dependency. C138SR-002: four units filed LATITUDE AS REQUIREMENTS - the fifth occurrence of the mixed obligation/latitude class, and notably the MIRROR of the sibling packet, which filed obligations as permission; all four were split into requirement and permission subunits. C138SR-003: an output-control facet sat under 13.9 p1, which owns only the input prohibition; output moved to p2. C138SR-004: a negative named a descriptor but NO DATUM, so nothing showed the p6 branch was reached; it now uses datum zero with (G4.1E3), where s=1 reaches the F branch, n=e+2=5 and w-n=-1, with repair (G7.1E3) expecting exactly '0.     ' - the reviewer derived all of that independently. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977.
